ko.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] "구매"를 누르기 전에: 뇌가 가장 먼저 밟는 세 단계

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > 대부분의 구매는 같은 경로를 따른다. 문제를 인식하고, 정보를 찾고, 선택지를 비교한다. 마케터는 이 모든 단계에 영향을 주려 한다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: 무언가를 사는 일은 한순간처럼 느껴질 수 있다. "주문하기"를 누르면 끝이다.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: 하지만 소비자심리학자들은 이것을 **과정**으로 설명한다.

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: 교과서적 설명에는 다섯 단계가 있다. 문제 인식, 정보 탐색, 대안 평가, 구매 결정, 구매 후 행동이다.

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: 이번 강의는 처음 세 단계를 다루는데, 실제로 고민과 결정이 대부분 일어나는 단계다.

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: 문제 인식**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: 모든 구매는 현재 상태(*실제 상태*)와 원하는 상태(*바람직한 상태*) 사이의 간격에서 시작된다.

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: 간격이 분명할 때도 있다. 휴대폰 화면이 깨지는 경우가 그렇다.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: 외부 요인이 간격을 만들기도 한다. 친구의 새 러닝화를 보고 내 운동화가 낡았다는 걸 갑자기 깨닫는 식이다.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: 광고는 이 단계에서 자주 작동한다.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: 광고가 늘 제품을 직접 파는 것은 아니다.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: 때로는 생각하지 못했던 간격을 알아차리게 만드는 것만으로도 충분하다.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: 정보 탐색**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: 필요를 인식하고 나면 그것을 충족할 방법을 찾는다.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: 탐색은 두 방향으로 이루어진다:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **내부 탐색:** 기억을 확인하기. "이 브랜드는 전에 써 봐서 만족했어."

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **외부 탐색:** 리뷰, 친구, 비교 사이트, 매장 방문, 영상 등 외부에서 정보를 찾기.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: 탐색의 양은 **관여도**에 따라 달라진다. 관여도란 구매가 얼마나 중요하고, 비싸고, 위험하게 느껴지는지를 뜻한다.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: 자동차를 사기 전에는 몇 주 동안 검색할 수도 있다.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: 껌 한 통을 살 때는 아마 전혀 검색하지 않을 것이다.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: 대안 평가**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: 이 시점에는 후보가 짧은 목록으로 줄어든다.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: 연구자들은 이것을 **고려 상품군**이라고 부른다. 존재하는 모든 선택지 가운데 실제로 진지하게 고려하는 몇몇 브랜드를 말한다.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: 소비자는 가격, 품질, 기능, 스타일 같은 **평가 기준**으로 이들을 비교한다.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: 어떤 사람은 모든 속성을 꼼꼼히 따진다.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: 하지만 더 흔하게는 정신적 지름길(**휴리스틱**)을 쓴다. 예를 들면 "예산 안에서 평점이 가장 좋은 것을 사자"거나 "아는 브랜드를 사자"는 식이다.

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: 브랜드가 고려 상품군에 들지 못하면 그 제품의 기능은 아무 의미가 없다. 그래서 많은 마케팅이 단순히 기억에 남는 것을 목표로 하는 이유가 여기에 있다.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: 이 과정은 늘 직선적이거나 의도적이지는 않다.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: 관여도가 낮거나 습관적인 구매에서는 사람들이 단계를 건너뛰거나 압축한다.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: 큰 구매에서는 흔히 앞 단계로 되돌아간다.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: 새 리뷰를 보면 다시 검색으로 돌아가기도 한다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상에서

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: 시카고에 살고 있는데 7월 폭염 중에 창문형 에어컨이 덜덜거리기 시작했다고 해 보자.

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **문제 인식:** 소음과 더운 바람 때문에 간격이 분명해진다. 덥고, 시원해지고 싶다. 이웃이 조용한 새 제품을 샀다고 말하면 그 간격이 더 크게 느껴진다.

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **정보 탐색:** 지난번 제품이 GE였고 몇 년이나 잘 썼다는 것을 기억한다(내부 탐색). 그다음 아마존과 Wirecutter에서 리뷰를 확인하고, 홈디포와 베스트바이에서 가격을 찾아보고, 최근에 산 친구에게 문자를 보낸다(외부 탐색).

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **대안 평가:** 고려 상품군은 280달러에서 450달러 사이 가격의 모델 세 개로 좁혀진다. BTU, 소음 수준, 에너지 효율을 비교한다. 결국 "400달러 이하에서 가장 조용한 제품"이라는 지름길을 쓴다. 그날 저녁 매장 픽업으로 주문한다.

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: 각 단계에서 브랜드는 영향을 줄 기회가 있었다. 시기를 잘 맞춘 여름 광고, 강한 리뷰, 또는 "같은 등급에서 가장 조용함"이라는 분명한 문구가 그 예다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. A purchase starts with **problem recognition**, the gap between your actual and desired state.
segments.tr: 1. 구매는 **문제 인식**, 즉 실제 상태와 원하는 상태 사이의 간격을 알아차리는 데서 시작한다.

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. 다음은 **정보 탐색**이다. 내부(기억)와 외부(리뷰, 사람, 매장) 탐색 모두 해당하며, 얼마나 찾을지는 관여도에 따라 달라진다.

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. **대안 평가**에서는 작은 고려 상품군을 기준과 흔히 정신적 지름길을 써서 비교한다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 점검

segments.src: (True/False)** Checking your memory of past experiences with a brand is an example of external search.
segments.tr: (참/거짓)** 어떤 브랜드에 대한 과거 경험을 기억 속에서 떠올리는 것은 외부 탐색의 예이다.

segments.src: (Multiple choice)** Which purchase would most likely involve the longest information search?
segments.tr: (객관식)** 다음 중 정보 탐색이 가장 길어질 가능성이 큰 구매는 무엇인가?

segments.src: - A) A bottle of water at a gas station
segments.tr: - A) 주유소에서 파는 생수 한 병

segments.src: - B) A new laptop for college
segments.tr: - B) 대학 신입생을 위한 새 노트북

segments.src: - C) Your usual brand of toothpaste
segments.tr: - C) 평소 쓰는 브랜드의 치약

segments.src: (Multiple choice)** The small group of brands a consumer seriously considers is called the:
segments.tr: (객관식)** 소비자가 진지하게 고려하는 소수의 브랜드 집합을 무엇이라 하는가?

segments.src: - A) Target market
segments.tr: - A) 표적 시장

segments.src: - B) Consideration set
segments.tr: - B) 고려 상품군

segments.src: - C) Brand portfolio
segments.tr: - C) 브랜드 포트폴리오

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** Noticing a meaningful gap between your current situation and the situation you want.
segments.tr: - **문제 인식:** 현재 상황과 원하는 상황 사이에서 의미 있는 간격을 알아차리는 것.

segments.src: - **Information search:** Looking for ways to close that gap, either through memory (internal) or outside sources (external).
segments.tr: - **정보 탐색:** 그 간격을 메우는 방법을 찾는 것. 기억(내부)을 통하거나 외부 자료(외부)를 통해 이루어진다.

segments.src: - **Involvement:** How personally important, costly, or risky a purchase feels. Higher involvement usually means more searching and comparing.
segments.tr: - **관여도:** 구매가 개인적으로 얼마나 중요하고, 비싸고, 위험하게 느껴지는지. 관여도가 높으면 보통 더 많이 탐색하고 비교한다.

segments.src: - **Consideration set:** The short list of brands or products a consumer actually considers buying.
segments.tr: - **고려 상품군:** 소비자가 실제로 구매를 고려하는 브랜드나 제품의 짧은 목록.

segments.src: - **Heuristic:** A mental shortcut that makes a decision quicker and easier, such as "buy the best-rated one."
segments.tr: - **휴리스틱:** "평점이 가장 좋은 것을 사자"처럼 결정을 더 빠르고 쉽게 만들어 주는 정신적 지름길.

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — False.
segments.tr: *정답: Q1 — 거짓.

segments.src: Searching your own memory is internal search.
segments.tr: 자기 기억을 떠올리는 것은 내부 탐색이다.

segments.src: External search uses outside sources like reviews or friends.
segments.tr: 외부 탐색은 리뷰나 친구 같은 외부 출처를 이용한다.

segments.src: Q2 — B.
segments.tr: Q2 — B.

segments.src: A laptop is expensive and important, so it's a high-involvement purchase that usually gets a lot of research.
segments.tr: 노트북은 비싸고 중요하므로 관여도가 높은 구매이며, 보통 많은 조사를 거친다.

segments.src: Q3 — B.
segments.tr: Q3 — B.

segments.src: The consideration set is the short list a buyer actually compares, and a brand that isn't on it rarely gets chosen.*
segments.tr: 고려 상품군은 구매자가 실제로 비교하는 짧은 목록이며, 이 목록에 없는 브랜드는 거의 선택되지 않는다.*

zh.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] 点击“购买”之前：你的大脑会先经历的三个步骤

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > 大多数购买都遵循相同的路径：你注意到一个问题，寻找信息，然后比较各种选项。营销人员会试图影响每一个步骤。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: 购买东西可能感觉只是一瞬间的事：你点击“下单”，就完成了。

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: 然而，消费心理学家把它描述为一个**过程**。

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: 教科书版本包含五个阶段：问题识别、信息搜索、备选方案评估、购买决策，以及购后行为。

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: 本课涵盖前三个阶段，大部分实际决策都发生在这里。

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: 问题识别**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: 每次购买都始于你所处的位置（你的*实际状态*）与你想要到达的位置（你的*期望状态*）之间的差距。

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: 有时这个差距很明显：你的手机屏幕裂了。

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: 另一些时候，差距来自外部，比如看到朋友的新跑鞋，突然意识到自己的鞋已经磨损了。

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: 广告通常在这一阶段发挥作用。

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: 它不一定直接推销产品。

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: 有时它只是让你意识到一个你从未想过的差距。

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: 信息搜索**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: 一旦意识到需求，你就会寻找满足它的方法。

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: 搜索有两个方向：

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **内部搜索：**回忆自己的记忆。“我以前用这个品牌体验很好。”

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **外部搜索：**向外寻找，例如评论、朋友、比价网站、实体店访问和视频。

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: 搜索的多少取决于**参与度**，即这次购买在你看来有多重要、多昂贵或多有风险。

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: 买车之前，你可能会搜索好几个星期。

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: 而买一包口香糖，你大概根本不会搜索。

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: 备选方案评估**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: 到了这一步，你手上已经有一份简短的清单。

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: 研究人员称之为**考虑集**：在所有存在的选项中，你会认真考虑的少数几个品牌。

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: 你会根据价格、质量、功能和风格等**评估标准**对它们进行比较。

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: 有些人会仔细权衡每一个属性。

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: 但更常见的是，我们会使用心理捷径（**启发式**），例如“我会在预算内选评分最高的那个”或“我就买我认识的品牌”。

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: 如果某个品牌从未进入你的考虑集，它的功能再好也无关紧要，这就是为什么如此多的营销只是为了让品牌被记住。

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: 这一过程并不总是线性的，也并非总是经过深思熟虑。

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: 对于低参与度或习惯性的购买，人们会跳过或压缩某些步骤。

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: 而对于大额购买，人们往往会反复回头。

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: 一条新的评论可能会让你重新开始搜索。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的例子

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: 假设你住在芝加哥，七月热浪来袭时，你的窗式空调开始嘎嘎作响。

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **问题识别：**噪音和热风造成了明显的差距。你觉得热，想要凉快。邻居提到他们新买的那台很安静，让这个差距感觉更大了。

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **信息搜索：**你记得上一台是 GE 的，用了好几年（内部搜索）。然后你在 Amazon 和 Wirecutter 上查看评论，在 Home Depot 和 Best Buy 上查价，并给刚买了一台的朋友发短信（外部搜索）。

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **备选方案评估：**你的考虑集最终是三款价格在 280 到 450 美元之间的机型。你比较了 BTU、噪音水平和能效。最后你用了一个捷径：“400 美元以下最安静的那台。”当晚你选择到店自提并下单。

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: 在每一步，都有一个品牌可能对你产生影响：一则恰逢夏季的广告、一条有力的评论，或一个清晰的“同类中最安静”标签。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: 1. A purchase starts with **problem recognition**, the gap between your actual and desired state.
segments.tr: 1. 购买始于**问题识别**，即实际状态与期望状态之间的差距。

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. 接下来是**信息搜索**，包括内部（记忆）和外部（评论、他人、商店）两种，搜索多少取决于参与度。

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. 在**备选方案评估**中，你会根据标准，通常还会借助心理捷径，来比较一个小的考虑集。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** Noticing a meaningful gap between your current situation and the situation you want.
segments.tr: - **问题识别：**注意到当前处境与你想要的处境之间存在有意义的差距。

segments.src: - **Information search:** Looking for ways to close that gap, either through memory (internal) or outside sources (external).
segments.tr: - **信息搜索：**寻找缩小这一差距的方法，可以通过记忆（内部），也可以通过外部来源（外部）。

segments.src: - **Involvement:** How personally important, costly, or risky a purchase feels. Higher involvement usually means more searching and comparing.
segments.tr: - **参与度：**一次购买在个人层面有多重要、多昂贵或多有风险。参与度越高，通常意味着搜索和比较越多。

segments.src: - **Consideration set:** The short list of brands or products a consumer actually considers buying.
segments.tr: - **考虑集：**消费者真正考虑购买的品牌或产品的简短清单。

segments.src: - **Heuristic:** A mental shortcut that makes a decision quicker and easier, such as "buy the best-rated one."
segments.tr: - **启发式：**一种让决策更快、更轻松的心理捷径，例如“买评分最高的那个”。

hi.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] "खरीदें" दबाने से पहले: आपका दिमाग जो तीन कदम पहले उठाता है

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > अधिकांश खरीदारियाँ एक ही क्रम का पालन करती हैं: आप किसी समस्या को पहचानते हैं, जानकारी खोजते हैं, और अपने विकल्पों की तुलना करते हैं। विपणक (मार्केटर) हर चरण को प्रभावित करने की कोशिश करते हैं।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: कोई चीज़ खरीदना एक ही पल जैसा लग सकता है: आप "Place Order" दबाते हैं और काम खत्म।

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: उपभोक्ता मनोवैज्ञानिक (consumer psychologists), हालाँकि, इसे एक **प्रक्रिया** के रूप में समझाते हैं।

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: पाठ्यपुस्तक के अनुसार इसके पाँच चरण हैं: समस्या की पहचान, जानकारी की खोज, विकल्पों का मूल्यांकन, खरीद का निर्णय, और खरीद के बाद का व्यवहार।

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: यह पाठ पहले तीन चरणों को समझाता है, जहाँ अधिकांश वास्तविक निर्णय लिया जाता है।

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: समस्या की पहचान**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: हर खरीद की शुरुआत उस अंतर से होती है जो आपकी *वास्तविक स्थिति* (actual state) और आपकी *वांछित स्थिति* (desired state) के बीच होता है।

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: कभी-कभी यह अंतर स्पष्ट होता है: आपके फ़ोन की स्क्रीन टूट जाती है।

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: कभी-कभी इसे आपके बाहर की कोई चीज़ पैदा करती है, जैसे किसी दोस्त के नए रनिंग शूज़ देखकर अचानक एहसास होना कि आपके अपने जूते घिस चुके हैं।

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: विज्ञापन अक्सर इसी चरण पर काम करता है।

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: यह हमेशा उत्पाद को सीधे नहीं बेचता।

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: कभी-कभी यह बस आपको ऐसे अंतर का एहसास कराता है जिसके बारे में आपने सोचा ही नहीं था।

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: जानकारी की खोज**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: जब आप किसी ज़रूरत को पहचान लेते हैं, तो उसे पूरा करने के तरीके खोजते हैं।

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: यह खोज दो दिशाओं में चलती है:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **आंतरिक खोज (internal search):** अपनी स्मृति को टटोलना। "इस ब्रांड का मेरा पहले भी अच्छा अनुभव रहा है।"

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **बाहरी खोज (external search):** बाहर की ओर देखना, जैसे समीक्षाएँ, दोस्त, तुलना वाली वेबसाइटें, स्टोर की यात्रा और वीडियो।

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: खोज कितनी होगी, यह **इन्वॉल्वमेंट (involvement)** पर निर्भर करता है, यानी खरीद कितनी महत्वपूर्ण, महँगी या जोखिम भरी लगती है।

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: कार खरीदने से पहले आप हफ्तों तक खोज कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: च्विंग गम के एक पैकेट के लिए शायद आप बिल्कुल खोज नहीं करते।

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: विकल्पों का मूल्यांकन**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: इस मोड़ पर आपके पास एक छोटी सूची होती है।

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: शोधकर्ता इसे **विचार-समुच्चय (consideration set)** कहते हैं: उन चुनिंदा ब्रांडों का समूह जिन पर आप गंभीरता से विचार करेंगे, मौजूद सभी विकल्पों में से।

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: आप इनकी तुलना **मूल्यांकन मानदंडों (evaluative criteria)** पर करते हैं, जैसे कीमत, गुणवत्ता, फीचर और शैली।

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: कुछ लोग हर विशेषता को ध्यान से तौलते हैं।

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: अधिक बार हम मानसिक शॉर्टकट (**हेयुरिस्टिक्स**) का उपयोग करते हैं, जैसे "मेरे बजट में जो सबसे अच्छी रेटिंग वाला हो, वही लूँगा" या "मैं बस वही ब्रांड लूँगा जिसे मैं जानता हूँ।"

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: अगर कोई ब्रांड आपके विचार-समुच्चय में कभी नहीं आता, तो उसके फीचर मायने नहीं रखते, इसीलिए इतनी सारी मार्केटिंग का लक्ष्य बस याद रखे जाना होता है।

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: यह प्रक्रिया हमेशा रैखिक या सोच-समझकर नहीं होती।

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: कम-इन्वॉल्वमेंट या आदतन खरीद में लोग कदम छोड़ देते हैं या समेट देते हैं।

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: बड़ी खरीद में वे अक्सर पीछे लौटते हैं।

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: कोई नई समीक्षा आपको फिर से खोज पर भेज सकती है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए आप शिकागो में रहते हैं और जुलाई की भीषण गर्मी में आपके अपार्टमेंट का विंडो एसी यूनिट खड़खड़ाने लगता है।

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **समस्या की पहचान:** शोर और गर्म हवा एक साफ़ अंतर पैदा करते हैं। आप गर्म हैं और ठंडक चाहते हैं। एक पड़ोसी का अपनी नई शांत यूनिट के बारे में बताना यह अंतर और बड़ा महसूस कराता है।

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **जानकारी की खोज:** आपको याद है कि आपकी पिछली यूनिट एक GE थी और वह सालों चली (आंतरिक खोज)। फिर आप Amazon और Wirecutter पर समीक्षाएँ देखते हैं, Home Depot और Best Buy पर कीमतें जाँचते हैं, और अभी-अभी एक खरीद चुके दोस्त को मैसेज करते हैं (बाहरी खोज)।

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **विकल्पों का मूल्यांकन:** आपके विचार-समुच्चय में अंत में तीन मॉडल रहते हैं जिनकी कीमत $280 से $450 है। आप BTU, शोर के स्तर और ऊर्जा दक्षता की तुलना करते हैं। आखिर में आप एक शॉर्टकट लेते हैं: "$400 से कम कीमत वाला सबसे शांत मॉडल।" आप उसे उसी शाम इन-स्टोर पिकअप के लिए ऑर्डर कर देते हैं।

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: हर चरण पर किसी ब्रांड को आप पर प्रभाव डालने का मौका मिला: समय पर चलाया गया गर्मी का विज्ञापन, एक मज़बूत समीक्षा, या "क्लास में सबसे शांत" जैसा साफ़ लेबल।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
1. A purchase starts with **problem recognition**, the gap between your actual and desired state.
segments.tr: 1. खरीद की शुरुआत **समस्या की पहचान** से होती है, यानी वास्तविक और वांछित स्थिति के बीच का अंतर।

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. इसके बाद **जानकारी की खोज** आती है, आंतरिक (स्मृति) और बाहरी (समीक्षाएँ, लोग, स्टोर) दोनों, और कितनी खोज होगी यह इन्वॉल्वमेंट पर निर्भर करता है।

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. **विकल्पों के मूल्यांकन** में आप मानदंडों और अक्सर मानसिक शॉर्टकट का उपयोग करके एक छोटे विचार-समुच्चय की तुलना करते हैं।

es.title: [Psicología del consumidor #9] Antes de hacer clic en «Comprar»: los tres pasos que tu cerebro da primero

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > La mayoría de las compras siguen el mismo camino: notas un problema, buscas información y comparas tus opciones. Los mercadólogos intentan influir en cada paso.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: Comprar algo puede parecer un momento único: pulsas «Realizar pedido» y ya está.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: Sin embargo, los psicólogos del consumidor lo describen como un **proceso**.

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: La versión de los libros de texto tiene cinco etapas: reconocimiento del problema, búsqueda de información, evaluación de alternativas, decisión de compra y comportamiento posterior a la compra.

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: Esta lección cubre las tres primeras, que es donde ocurre la mayor parte de la decisión real.

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: Reconocimiento del problema**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: Toda compra comienza con una brecha entre dónde estás (tu *estado real*) y dónde quieres estar (tu *estado deseado*).

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: A veces la brecha es obvia: se te rompe la pantalla del teléfono.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: Otras veces la crea algo externo, como ver las zapatillas de correr nuevas de un amigo y darte cuenta de repente de que las tuyas están gastadas.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: La publicidad suele funcionar en esta etapa.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: No siempre vende un producto directamente.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: A veces simplemente te hace notar una brecha en la que no habías pensado.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: Búsqueda de información**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: Una vez que reconoces una necesidad, buscas formas de satisfacerla.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: La búsqueda avanza en dos direcciones:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **Búsqueda interna:** revisar tu memoria. «Ya tuve una buena experiencia con esta marca.»

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **Búsqueda externa:** mirar hacia fuera: reseñas, amigos, sitios comparativos, visitas a tiendas y videos.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: La cantidad de búsqueda depende de la **implicación**, es decir, de cuán importante, costosa o arriesgada te parece la compra.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: Puedes buscar durante semanas antes de comprar un coche.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: Para un paquete de chicle probablemente no buscas nada.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: Evaluación de alternativas**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: En este punto tienes una lista corta.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: Los investigadores la llaman **conjunto de consideración**: el puñado de marcas en las que pensarías seriamente, de entre todas las opciones que existen.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: Las comparas según **criterios de evaluación**, como precio, calidad, características y estilo.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: Algunas personas sopesan cuidadosamente cada atributo.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: Con más frecuencia usamos atajos mentales (**heurísticos**), como «compraré la mejor valorada dentro de mi presupuesto» o «compraré simplemente la marca que conozco».

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: Si una marca nunca entra en tu conjunto de consideración, sus características no importan, por eso tanto marketing apunta simplemente a ser recordado.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: El proceso no siempre es lineal ni deliberado.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: En compras de baja implicación o habituales, la gente omite o comprime pasos.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: En compras grandes, suelen volver atrás.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: Una nueva reseña puede hacerte regresar a la búsqueda.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: Supongamos que vives en Chicago y el aire acondicionado de ventana de tu apartamento empieza a traquetear durante una ola de calor de julio.

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **Reconocimiento del problema:** El ruido y el aire caliente crean una brecha clara. Tienes calor y quieres estar fresco. Que un vecino mencione su nuevo equipo silencioso hace que la brecha parezca mayor.

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **Búsqueda de información:** Recuerdas que tu equipo anterior era un GE y duró años (búsqueda interna). Luego revisas reseñas en Amazon y Wirecutter, consultas precios en Home Depot y Best Buy, y le escribes a un amigo que acaba de comprar uno (búsqueda externa).

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **Evaluación de alternativas:** Tu conjunto de consideración queda en tres modelos con precios de $280 a $450. Comparas BTU, nivel de ruido y eficiencia energética. Al final usas un atajo: «el más silencioso por menos de $400». Lo pides para recoger en tienda esa misma tarde.

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: En cada paso, una marca tuvo la oportunidad de influir en ti: un anuncio de verano bien colocado, una reseña sólida o una etiqueta clara de «el más silencioso de su categoría».

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumen en 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. A purchase starts with **problem recognition**, the gap between your actual and desired state.
segments.tr: 1. Una compra comienza con el **reconocimiento del problema**, la brecha entre tu estado real y tu estado deseado.

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. Después viene la **búsqueda de información**, tanto interna (memoria) como externa (reseñas, personas, tiendas), y cuánto buscas depende de la implicación.

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. En la **evaluación de alternativas**, comparas un pequeño conjunto de consideración usando criterios y, con frecuencia, atajos mentales.

fr.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] Avant de cliquer sur « Acheter » : les trois étapes que votre cerveau franchit en premier

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > La plupart des achats suivent le même chemin : vous remarquez un problème, cherchez des informations et comparez vos options. Les marketeurs tentent d'influencer chaque étape.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: Acheter un article peut sembler être un moment unique : vous appuyez sur « Passer la commande » et c'est terminé.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: Les psychologues du consommateur, en revanche, le décrivent comme un **processus**.

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: La version des manuels compte cinq étapes : la reconnaissance du problème, la recherche d'informations, l'évaluation des alternatives, la décision d'achat et le comportement après l'achat.

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: Cette leçon traite des trois premières, où se joue l'essentiel de la décision.

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: Reconnaissance du problème**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: Tout achat commence par un écart entre là où vous êtes (votre *état actuel*) et là où vous voulez être (votre *état souhaité*).

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: Parfois, l'écart est évident : l'écran de votre téléphone se fissure.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: D'autres fois, c'est un élément extérieur qui le crée, comme voir les nouvelles chaussures de course d'un ami et remarquer soudain que les vôtres sont usées.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: La publicité agit souvent à ce stade.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: Elle ne vend pas toujours un produit directement.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: Parfois, elle vous fait simplement remarquer un écart auquel vous n'aviez pas pensé.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: Recherche d'informations**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: Une fois le besoin identifié, vous cherchez des moyens de le satisfaire.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: La recherche s'effectue dans deux directions :

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **Recherche interne :** consulter votre mémoire. « J'ai déjà eu une bonne expérience avec cette marque. »

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **Recherche externe :** se tourner vers les avis, les amis, les comparateurs, les visites en magasin et les vidéos.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: L'ampleur de la recherche dépend de l'**implication**, c'est-à-dire du degré d'importance, de coût ou de risque que représente l'achat.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: Vous pouvez chercher pendant des semaines avant d'acheter une voiture.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: Pour un paquet de chewing-gum, vous ne cherchez probablement pas du tout.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: Évaluation des alternatives**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: À ce stade, vous avez une courte liste.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: Les chercheurs l'appellent l'**ensemble de considération** : la poignée de marques que vous envisageriez sérieusement, parmi toutes les options existantes.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: Vous les comparez selon des **critères d'évaluation** tels que le prix, la qualité, les fonctionnalités et le style.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: Certaines personnes pèsent soigneusement chaque caractéristique.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: Plus souvent, nous utilisons des raccourcis mentaux (**heuristiques**), comme « je prendrai le mieux noté dans mon budget » ou « j'achèterai simplement la marque que je connais. »

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: Si une marque n'entre jamais dans votre ensemble de considération, ses caractéristiques n'ont pas d'importance ; c'est pourquoi tant de marketing vise simplement à être mémorisé.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: Le processus n'est pas toujours linéaire ni délibéré.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: Pour les achats à faible implication ou habituels, les gens sautent ou compressent des étapes.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: Pour les gros achats, ils reviennent souvent en arrière.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: Un nouvel avis peut vous renvoyer à la recherche.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie de tous les jours

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: Imaginons que vous vivez à Chicago et que le climatiseur de la fenêtre de votre appartement se met à cliqueter pendant une vague de chaleur en juillet.

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **Reconnaissance du problème :** le bruit et l'air chaud créent un écart clair. Vous avez chaud et voulez être au frais. Un voisin qui mentionne son nouvel appareil silencieux rend cet écart encore plus sensible.

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **Recherche d'informations :** vous vous souvenez que votre dernier appareil était une GE et qu'il a duré des années (recherche interne). Vous consultez ensuite les avis sur Amazon et Wirecutter, regardez les prix chez Home Depot et Best Buy, et envoyez un SMS à un ami qui vient d'en acheter un (recherche externe).

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **Évaluation des alternatives :** votre ensemble de considération se réduit à trois modèles, à des prix allant de 280 à 450 $. Vous comparez les BTU, le niveau sonore et l'efficacité énergétique. Au final, vous utilisez un raccourci : « le plus silencieux à moins de 400 $ ». Vous le commandez pour le retirer en magasin le soir même.

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: À chaque étape, une marque a eu une chance de vous influencer : une publicité estivale bien placée, un avis élogieux ou une mention claire « le plus silencieux de sa catégorie ».

segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.tr: 1. Un achat commence par la **reconnaissance du problème**, l'écart entre votre état actuel et votre état souhaité.

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. Vient ensuite la **recherche d'informations**, à la fois interne (mémoire) et externe (avis, personnes, magasins) ; l'ampleur de la recherche dépend de l'implication.

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. Lors de l'**évaluation des alternatives**, vous comparez un petit ensemble de considération à l'aide de critères et, souvent, de raccourcis mentaux.

in.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] Sebelum Anda Klik "Beli": Tiga Langkah yang Pertama Kali Dilakukan Otak Anda

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > Sebagian besar pembelian mengikuti jalur yang sama: Anda menyadari suatu masalah, mencari informasi, dan membandingkan pilihan. Pemasar berusaha memengaruhi setiap langkah.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: Membeli sesuatu bisa terasa seperti satu momen saja: Anda menekan "Pesan Sekarang" dan selesai.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: Namun, psikolog konsumen menggambarkannya sebagai **proses**.

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: Versi buku teks memiliki lima tahap: pengenalan masalah, pencarian informasi, evaluasi alternatif, keputusan pembelian, dan perilaku pascapembelian.

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: Pelajaran ini membahas tiga tahap pertama, yang merupakan tempat sebagian besar pengambilan keputusan sebenarnya terjadi.

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: Pengenalan masalah**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: Setiap pembelian dimulai dari kesenjangan antara kondisi Anda saat ini (*kondisi aktual*) dan kondisi yang Anda inginkan (*kondisi yang diinginkan*).

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: Kadang kesenjangan itu jelas: layar ponsel Anda retak.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: Di lain waktu, sesuatu dari luar yang menciptakannya, misalnya melihat sepatu lari baru milik teman dan tiba-tiba menyadari bahwa sepatu Anda sudah aus.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: Iklan sering bekerja pada tahap ini.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: Iklan tidak selalu menjual produk secara langsung.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: Kadang iklan hanya membuat Anda menyadari kesenjangan yang sebelumnya tidak Anda pikirkan.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: Pencarian informasi**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: Setelah Anda menyadari kebutuhan, Anda mencari cara untuk memenuhinya.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: Pencarian berjalan ke dua arah:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **Pencarian internal:** memeriksa ingatan Anda. "Saya pernah punya pengalaman baik dengan merek ini."

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **Pencarian eksternal:** mencari ke luar, seperti ulasan, teman, situs perbandingan, kunjungan ke toko, dan video.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: Seberapa banyak pencarian yang dilakukan bergantung pada **keterlibatan**, yaitu seberapa penting, mahal, atau berisiko pembelian itu terasa.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: Anda mungkin mencari selama berminggu-minggu sebelum membeli mobil.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: Untuk sebungkus permen karet, Anda mungkin sama sekali tidak mencari.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: Evaluasi alternatif**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: Pada titik ini Anda sudah punya daftar pendek.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: Para peneliti menyebutnya **kumpulan pertimbangan**: sekumpulan kecil merek yang benar-benar akan Anda pikirkan, dari sekian banyak pilihan yang ada.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: Anda membandingkannya berdasarkan **kriteria evaluatif** seperti harga, kualitas, fitur, dan gaya.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: Sebagian orang menimbang setiap atribut dengan cermat.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: Namun, lebih sering kita memakai jalan pintas mental (**heuristik**), seperti "Saya akan membeli yang peringkatnya terbaik dalam anggaran saya" atau "Saya akan membeli merek yang saya kenal saja."

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: Jika sebuah merek tidak pernah masuk ke kumpulan pertimbangan Anda, fitur-fiturnya tidak lagi berarti, itulah sebabnya banyak pemasaran berusaha agar sekadar diingat.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: Proses ini tidak selalu linear atau disengaja.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: Pada pembelian dengan keterlibatan rendah atau yang sudah menjadi kebiasaan, orang melewati atau memadatkan langkah.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: Pada pembelian besar, mereka sering kembali ke tahap sebelumnya.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: Ulasan baru bisa membuat Anda kembali mencari informasi.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: 代替案の評価**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: この時点で、候補はある程度絞られています。

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: 研究者はこれを**検討集合**と呼びます。存在するすべての選択肢のうち、真剣に検討する少数のブランドの集まりです。

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: 価格、品質、機能、デザインなどの**評価基準**に基づいて比較します。

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: すべての属性を慎重に比較する人もいます。

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: しかし実際には、「予算内で最も評価の高いものにしよう」「知っているブランドを買おう」といった心理的な近道（**ヒューリスティック**）を使うことの方が多いものです。

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: あるブランドが検討集合に入らなければ、その機能がどれほど優れていても意味がありません。だからこそ多くのマーケティングは、ただ「覚えてもらう」ことを目指すのです。

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: このプロセスは、必ずしも直線的でも意図的でもありません。

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: 関与度の低い購買や習慣的な購買では、人はステップを飛ばしたり、短縮したりします。

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: 大きな買い物では、しばしば前の段階に戻ります。

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: 新しいレビューを見て、再び情報探索に戻ることもあります。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活での例

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **情報探索:** 以前使っていた機種はGE製で、何年も使えたことを思い出します（内部探索）。次にAmazonやWirecutterでレビューを確認し、Home DepotやBest Buyで価格を調べ、最近購入した友人にメッセージを送ります（外部探索）。

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: どの段階でも、ブランドが影響を与える機会がありました。タイミングのよい夏の広告、高評価のレビュー、そして「クラス最静音」という分かりやすい表示などです。

de.title: [Consumer Psychology #9] Bevor du auf „Kaufen“ klickst: Die drei Schritte, die dein Gehirn zuerst durchläuft

segments.src: > Most purchases follow the same path: you notice a problem, look for information, and compare your options. Marketers try to influence every step.
segments.tr: > Die meisten Käufe folgen demselben Ablauf: Du bemerkst ein Problem, suchst nach Informationen und vergleichst deine Optionen. Vermarkter versuchen, jeden dieser Schritte zu beeinflussen.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Das heutige Konzept

segments.src: Buying something can feel like a single moment: you tap "Place Order" and you're done.
segments.tr: Ein Kauf kann wie ein einziger Moment wirken: Du tippst auf „Bestellung aufgeben“ und bist fertig.

segments.src: Consumer psychologists, however, describe it as a **process**.
segments.tr: Konsumpsychologen beschreiben ihn jedoch als **Prozess**.

segments.src: The textbook version has five stages: problem recognition, information search, evaluation of alternatives, the purchase decision, and post-purchase behavior.
segments.tr: Das Lehrbuch unterscheidet fünf Phasen: Problemerkennung, Informationssuche, Bewertung von Alternativen, die Kaufentscheidung und das Verhalten nach dem Kauf.

segments.src: This lesson covers the first three, where most of the actual deciding happens.
segments.tr: Diese Lektion behandelt die ersten drei, in denen der größte Teil der eigentlichen Entscheidung fällt.

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: Problemerkennung**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: Jeder Kauf beginnt mit einer Lücke zwischen dem, wo du gerade stehst (dein *Ist-Zustand*), und dem, wo du hinwillst (dein *Soll-Zustand*).

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: Manchmal ist die Lücke offensichtlich: Dein Handybildschirm ist gesprungen.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: Manchmal entsteht sie durch äußere Einflüsse, etwa wenn du die neuen Laufschuhe eines Freundes siehst und plötzlich merkst, dass deine eigenen abgenutzt sind.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: Werbung wirkt in dieser Phase oft.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: Sie verkauft nicht immer direkt ein Produkt.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: Manchmal bringt sie dich nur dazu, eine Lücke zu bemerken, an die du nicht gedacht hattest.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: Informationssuche**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: Sobald du einen Bedarf erkannt hast, suchst du nach Wegen, ihn zu decken.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: Die Suche verläuft in zwei Richtungen:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **Interne Suche:** Du prüfst dein Gedächtnis. „Mit dieser Marke habe ich schon gute Erfahrungen gemacht.“

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **Externe Suche:** Du wendest dich nach außen, zu Bewertungen, Freunden, Vergleichsportalen, Ladenbesuchen und Videos.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: Wie viel gesucht wird, hängt vom **Involvement** ab, also davon, wie wichtig, teuer oder riskant sich der Kauf anfühlt.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: Vor dem Kauf eines Autos kann man wochenlang suchen.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: Für eine Packung Kaugummi sucht man vermutlich gar nicht.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: Bewertung von Alternativen**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: Jetzt hast du eine kurze Liste.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: Forscher nennen sie das **Consideration Set**: die Handvoll Marken, die du ernsthaft in Betracht ziehst, von allen verfügbaren Optionen.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: Du vergleichst sie anhand **Bewertungskriterien** wie Preis, Qualität, Funktionen und Stil.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: Manche Menschen wägen jedes Merkmal sorgfältig ab.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: Häufiger nutzen wir mentale Abkürzungen (**Heuristiken**), etwa „Ich nehme das bestbewertete Produkt in meinem Budget“ oder „Ich kaufe einfach die Marke, die ich kenne“.

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: Wenn es eine Marke nie in dein Consideration Set schafft, spielen ihre Funktionen keine Rolle. Deshalb zielt so viel Marketing einfach darauf ab, im Gedächtnis zu bleiben.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: Der Prozess verläuft nicht immer linear oder bewusst.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: Bei Käufen mit geringem Involvement oder Routinekäufen überspringen Menschen Schritte oder verkürzen sie.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: Bei großen Käufen kehren sie oft zurück.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: Eine neue Bewertung kann dich wieder zur Suche zurückschicken.

Dann liest du Bewertungen auf Amazon und Wirecutter, schaust Preise bei Home Depot und Best Buy nach und schreibst einem Freund, der gerade eins gekauft hat (externe Suche).

segments.src: Problem recognition**
segments.tr: Nhận diện vấn đề**

segments.src: Every purchase starts with a gap between where you are (your *actual state*) and where you want to be (your *desired state*).
segments.tr: Mọi lần mua hàng đều bắt đầu từ khoảng cách giữa nơi bạn đang ở (*trạng thái thực tế*) và nơi bạn muốn đến (*trạng thái mong muốn*).

segments.src: Sometimes the gap is obvious: your phone screen cracks.
segments.tr: Đôi khi khoảng cách rất rõ ràng: màn hình điện thoại bị nứt.

segments.src: Other times something outside you creates it, like seeing a friend's new running shoes and suddenly noticing that yours are worn out.
segments.tr: Có lúc khoảng cách được tạo ra từ bên ngoài, chẳng hạn khi thấy đôi giày chạy bộ mới của bạn bè và đột nhiên nhận ra đôi giày của mình đã cũ.

segments.src: Advertising often works at this stage.
segments.tr: Quảng cáo thường phát huy tác dụng ở giai đoạn này.

segments.src: It doesn't always sell a product directly.
segments.tr: Nó không phải lúc nào cũng bán sản phẩm một cách trực tiếp.

segments.src: Sometimes it just makes you notice a gap you hadn't thought about.
segments.tr: Đôi khi nó chỉ khiến bạn nhận ra một khoảng cách mà trước đó bạn chưa từng nghĩ tới.

segments.src: Information search**
segments.tr: Tìm kiếm thông tin**

segments.src: Once you've recognized a need, you look for ways to meet it.
segments.tr: Khi đã nhận ra nhu cầu, bạn sẽ tìm cách đáp ứng nó.

segments.src: The search runs in two directions:
segments.tr: Việc tìm kiếm diễn ra theo hai hướng:

segments.src: - **Internal search:** checking your memory. "I've had a good experience with this brand before."
segments.tr: - **Tìm kiếm nội bộ:** kiểm tra trí nhớ của bạn. “Tôi từng có trải nghiệm tốt với thương hiệu này.”

segments.src: - **External search:** looking outward to reviews, friends, comparison sites, store visits, and videos.
segments.tr: - **Tìm kiếm bên ngoài:** tìm kiếm từ các nguồn như đánh giá, bạn bè, trang so sánh, việc ghé cửa hàng và video.

segments.src: The amount of searching depends on **involvement**, meaning how important, expensive, or risky the purchase feels.
segments.tr: Mức độ tìm kiếm phụ thuộc vào **mức độ liên quan** (involvement), tức là món hàng quan trọng, đắt tiền hoặc rủi ro đến mức nào.

segments.src: You might search for weeks before buying a car.
segments.tr: Bạn có thể tìm hiểu trong nhiều tuần trước khi mua một chiếc ô tô.

segments.src: For a pack of gum you probably don't search at all.
segments.tr: Còn với một gói kẹo cao su, bạn có lẽ hoàn toàn không tìm kiếm gì.

segments.src: Evaluation of alternatives**
segments.tr: Đánh giá các phương án**

segments.src: At this point you have a short list.
segments.tr: Lúc này bạn đã có một danh sách ngắn.

segments.src: Researchers call it the **consideration set**: the handful of brands you'd seriously think about, out of all the options that exist.
segments.tr: Các nhà nghiên cứu gọi đó là **tập cân nhắc** (consideration set): một số ít thương hiệu mà bạn thực sự sẽ cân nhắc, trong vô số lựa chọn có trên thị trường.

segments.src: You compare them on **evaluative criteria** such as price, quality, features, and style.
segments.tr: Bạn so sánh chúng theo **tiêu chí đánh giá** như giá cả, chất lượng, tính năng và kiểu dáng.

segments.src: Some people weigh every attribute carefully.
segments.tr: Có người cân nhắc kỹ từng thuộc tính.

segments.src: More often we use mental shortcuts (**heuristics**), such as "I'll get the best-rated one under my budget" or "I'll just buy the brand I know."
segments.tr: Nhưng thường thì chúng ta dùng các lối tắt nhận thức (**heuristic**), chẳng hạn “Tôi sẽ chọn món được đánh giá cao nhất trong ngân sách” hoặc “Tôi cứ mua thương hiệu mình biết.”

segments.src: If a brand never makes it into your consideration set, its features don't matter, which is why so much marketing aims simply to be remembered.
segments.tr: Nếu một thương hiệu không bao giờ lọt vào tập cân nhắc của bạn, thì các tính năng của nó cũng không còn quan trọng, và đó là lý do vì sao rất nhiều hoạt động tiếp thị chỉ nhằm mục đích được ghi nhớ.

segments.src: The process isn't always linear or deliberate.
segments.tr: Quá trình này không phải lúc nào cũng tuyến tính hay có chủ đích.

segments.src: With low-involvement or habitual purchases, people skip or compress steps.
segments.tr: Với những lần mua ít liên quan hoặc mang tính thói quen, người ta thường bỏ qua hoặc rút ngắn các bước.

segments.src: With big purchases, they often loop back.
segments.tr: Với những lần mua lớn, họ thường quay lại các bước trước đó.

segments.src: A new review can send you back to searching.
segments.tr: Một đánh giá mới có thể khiến bạn quay lại tìm kiếm.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong đời sống hằng ngày

segments.src: Say you live in Chicago and your apartment's window AC unit starts rattling during a July heat wave.
segments.tr: Giả sử bạn sống ở Chicago và chiếc máy điều hòa cửa sổ trong căn hộ bắt đầu kêu lạch cạch trong đợt nắng nóng tháng Bảy.

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** The noise and warm air create a clear gap. You're hot and you want to be cool. A neighbor mentioning their quiet new unit makes the gap feel bigger.
segments.tr: - **Nhận diện vấn đề:** Tiếng ồn và luồng không khí nóng tạo ra một khoảng cách rõ rệt. Bạn đang nóng và muốn mát hơn. Việc hàng xóm nhắc đến chiếc máy mới êm ái của họ khiến khoảng cách đó càng lớn hơn.

segments.src: - **Information search:** You remember that your last unit was a GE and it lasted years (internal search). Then you check reviews on Amazon and Wirecutter, look up prices at Home Depot and Best Buy, and text a friend who just bought one (external search).
segments.tr: - **Tìm kiếm thông tin:** Bạn nhớ chiếc máy trước đây của mình là GE và đã dùng được nhiều năm (tìm kiếm nội bộ). Sau đó bạn xem đánh giá trên Amazon và Wirecutter, tra giá ở Home Depot và Best Buy, rồi nhắn tin hỏi một người bạn vừa mua một chiếc (tìm kiếm bên ngoài).

segments.src: - **Evaluation of alternatives:** Your consideration set ends up as three models priced from $280 to $450. You compare BTUs, noise level, and energy efficiency. In the end you use a shortcut: "the quietest one under $400." You order it for in-store pickup that evening.
segments.tr: - **Đánh giá các phương án:** Tập cân nhắc của bạn cuối cùng gồm ba mẫu có giá từ 280 đến 450 USD. Bạn so sánh BTU, độ ồn và hiệu suất năng lượng. Cuối cùng bạn dùng một lối tắt: “chiếc êm nhất dưới 400 USD.” Bạn đặt mua để nhận tại cửa hàng vào tối hôm đó.

segments.src: At each step, a brand had a chance to influence you: a well-timed summer ad, a strong review, or a clear "quietest in class" label.
segments.tr: Ở mỗi bước, một thương hiệu đều có cơ hội tác động đến bạn: một quảng cáo mùa hè đúng thời điểm, một đánh giá tốt, hoặc một nhãn “êm nhất trong phân khúc” rõ ràng.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm tắt trong 3 dòng

segments.src: 1. A purchase starts with **problem recognition**, the gap between your actual and desired state.
segments.tr: 1. Một lần mua bắt đầu từ **nhận diện vấn đề**, tức khoảng cách giữa trạng thái thực tế và trạng thái mong muốn của bạn.

segments.src: 2. Next comes **information search**, both internal (memory) and external (reviews, people, stores), and how much you search depends on involvement.
segments.tr: 2. Tiếp theo là **tìm kiếm thông tin**, cả nội bộ (trí nhớ) lẫn bên ngoài (đánh giá, người quen, cửa hàng), và mức độ tìm kiếm phụ thuộc vào mức độ liên quan.

segments.src: 3. In **evaluation of alternatives**, you compare a small consideration set using criteria and, often, mental shortcuts.
segments.tr: 3. Trong **đánh giá các phương án**, bạn so sánh một tập cân nhắc nhỏ bằng các tiêu chí và thường là cả các lối tắt nhận thức.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Thuật ngữ hôm nay

segments.src: - **Problem recognition:** Noticing a meaningful gap between your current situation and the situation you want.
segments.tr: - **Nhận diện vấn đề:** Nhận ra một khoảng cách đáng kể giữa tình huống hiện tại và tình huống bạn mong muốn.

segments.src: - **Information search:** Looking for ways to close that gap, either through memory (internal) or outside sources (external).
segments.tr: - **Tìm kiếm thông tin:** Tìm cách thu hẹp khoảng cách đó, thông qua trí nhớ (nội bộ) hoặc các nguồn bên ngoài.

segments.src: - **Involvement:** How personally important, costly, or risky a purchase feels. Higher involvement usually means more searching and comparing.
segments.tr: - **Mức độ liên quan (involvement):** Mức độ một lần mua quan trọng, tốn kém hoặc rủi ro đối với cá nhân. Mức độ liên quan càng cao thì thường càng phải tìm kiếm và so sánh nhiều hơn.

segments.src: - **Consideration set:** The short list of brands or products a consumer actually considers buying.
segments.tr: - **Tập cân nhắc:** Danh sách ngắn các thương hiệu hoặc sản phẩm mà người tiêu dùng thực sự cân nhắc mua.

segments.src: - **Heuristic:** A mental shortcut that makes a decision quicker and easier, such as "buy the best-rated one."
segments.tr: - **Heuristic:** Một lối tắt nhận thức giúp việc ra quyết định nhanh hơn và dễ hơn, chẳng hạn “mua món được đánh giá cao nhất.”

segments.src: *Answers: Q1 — False.
segments.tr: *Đáp án: Q1 — Sai.

segments.src: Searching your own memory is internal search.
segments.tr: Tìm kiếm trong trí nhớ của chính bạn là tìm kiếm nội bộ.

segments.src: External search uses outside sources like reviews or friends.
segments.tr: Tìm kiếm bên ngoài sử dụng các nguồn từ bên ngoài như đánh giá hoặc bạn bè.

segments.src: Q2 — B.
segments.tr: Q2 — B.

segments.src: A laptop is expensive and important, so it's a high-involvement purchase that usually gets a lot of research.
segments.tr: Laptop là sản phẩm đắt tiền và quan trọng, nên đây là lần mua có mức độ liên quan cao, thường được nghiên cứu kỹ.

segments.src: Q3 — B.
segments.tr: Q3 — B.

segments.src: The consideration set is the short list a buyer actually compares, and a brand that isn't on it rarely gets chosen.*
segments.tr: Tập cân nhắc là danh sách ngắn mà người mua thực sự so sánh, và một thương hiệu không nằm trong danh sách đó hiếm khi được chọn.*
